gaps.lead: You can't park here — it's forbidden.
gaps.explanation: mustn't = it is forbidden (not: don't have to).

gaps.lead: 'Could you pass the salt?' said my aunt to me.
gaps.explanation: Reported request: asked me to pass.

gaps.lead: Although he is rich, he lives very simply.
gaps.explanation: Although he may be rich → Rich as (he) may be — the inverted concession pattern.

gaps.lead: 'You mustn't run near the pool,' the lifeguard told the children.
gaps.sentence: The lifeguard told the children ___ near the pool.

gaps.lead: They left the party early because it was boring.
gaps.sentence: The party was ___ that they left early.
gaps.explanation: so + adjective + that-clause: so boring that they left.

gaps.lead: It isn't necessary for you to bring any food.
gaps.explanation: needn't (need not) = it isn't necessary. Do not confuse with mustn't (prohibition).
